result.title: MotifFlow: Training-Free, Self-Contained Style Transfer from Color to Motif in Rectified Flow Transformers
result.summary: Expressive style transfer must reproduce a painting's palette, brushwork, and characteristic motifs while retaining the content image's structure. Attention injection is effective in U-Net-based diffusion models, but adapting it to FLUX often transfers color without capturing the style's distinctive brushwork. Our analysis across backbones links this gap to how injected features are integrated across neighboring spatial locations. We introduce MotifFlow, a training-free, self-contained framework that combines style injection with style-alignment guidance in FLUX. Injection supplies style features during generation but does not explicitly encourage the model's native attention output to align with them. We therefore use the discrepancy between native and injected attention outputs to guide latent-space updates, encouraging the evolving image to develop the style's distinctive brushwork and motifs. Style encoding, guidance, and synthesis all use the same frozen backbone, without auxiliary image encoders or trained adapters. A single strength parameter controls the transition from color transfer to pronounced brushwork and motifs, with additional support for regional stylization and style mixing. Experiments on 1,000 content-style pairs show that MotifFlow better matches the local textures of the style image than baseline methods and produces more consistent stylization than injection alone. The same design extends to FLUX.2.

AI.brief_summary: MotifFlow 提出免训练的风格迁移框架，在 FLUX 中将风格注意力注入与「原生注意力与注入注意力输出差异」引导的 latent 更新结合，实现从色彩到笔触与母题的迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作面向图像风格化生成，其中的 latent 指扩散噪声状态而非推理状态，材料未涉及视觉证据筛选、推理步数或答案使用等主线问题，差异引导更新与 LVR 状态监督的联系过于间接，故排除。
